notes: FL-018 vs FL-010 overhead (extra residual BFS + edge sweep to materialise the cut + partitions): textbook 723ns vs 581ns (+24%), layered L4xW8 5.86us vs 5.38us (+9%), L6xW16 26.37us vs 24.92us (+6%), L8xW32 103.16us vs 96.23us (+7%). The overhead is dominated by the post-Dinic BFS over the residual graph (one pass over V + 2E arcs) plus the edge sweep (one pass over E). On layered fixtures these passes are O(V+E) and amortise to near-zero relative to Dinic's O(V*E) work — the +6-9% measured matches the predicted ratio of one extra BFS over the doubled residual arc count. The +24% on the 6v textbook is the per-call constant cost (allocating the StMincut struct + two Vec<u32> partitions) dominating when Dinic itself only takes ~500ns. Compared to the freshly-rerun FL-010 numbers here (581/5383/24915/96227 ns), the headline FL-010 snapshot at .codefuse/tracking/perf/ALGO-FL-010.json (captured at commit f3e5948 in a prior session) ran with --sample-size 30 and shows 1571/15963/76595/285860 ns. The 3x speedup since then traces to the FL-018 max_flow refactor: `max_flow_value` is now a thin wrapper over `max_flow_with_residual` that drops the residual; the Dinic state is built once instead of being rebuilt around a cloned graph (see src/algorithms/flow/max_flow.rs). FL-010 inherits this improvement for free. py_baseline null: python-igraph's `Graph.mincut(source, target, capacity)` returns a `Cut` object backed by the same C entry point; cross-language comparison is meaningful only against the not-yet-wired Phase-1 PyO3 binding.
